expectations.text: Running the skill's scripts/check_app.R on the produced app directory reports 0 errors.
Column dropdown choices are filled from the uploaded file's columns (updateSelectInput/updateSelectizeInput or renderUI), with the numeric dropdown limited to numeric columns.
expectations.evidence: observeEvent(data()) -> updateSelectInput value (numeric columns only) and group (all columns, default first non-numeric-first column = Diet).

expectations.text: Code reads input$<file>$datapath and guards with req() so nothing errors before a file is uploaded.
expectations.evidence: data() starts with req(input$file) then read.csv(input$file$datapath); pre-upload outputs are silent errors, no R error.

expectations.text: Summary statistics use na.rm = TRUE (or equivalent) and report a per-group count of missing values; on chick_weights.csv the weight column shows 6 missing in total.
expectations.evidence: group_summary: missing = sum(is.na(v)), mean/sd na.rm=TRUE; testServer weight by Diet missing 2,2,0,2 = 6.

expectations.text: When the report download is triggered with chick_weights.csv uploaded (e.g. via testServer), an HTML file is produced that contains the summary table and an embedded plot.
expectations.evidence: output$report via testServer produced HTML (81 KB) with kable (n/missing/mean/sd rows, e.g. 218/2/102.36/56.63) and from ggsave + knitr::image_uri.

expectations.text: The report is rendered from a template copied to tempdir() (or otherwise not written into the app folder) and receives data via params or an explicit environment, not via global variables.
expectations.evidence: No template and no params/environment: the HTML is assembled with paste0() inside downloadHandler from reactives. It does write only to tempfile()/file (app dir unchanged) and uses no globals, but the assertion's template + params/env mechanism is absent.

expectations.text: Uploading a CSV that has no numeric column shows a readable message in the page (validate/need, showNotification or similar that is actually displayed) rather than a blank page or an R error.
expectations.evidence: name,city CSV: showNotification('The file has no numeric columns.', type='error') called (captured via session$sendNotification). Outputs themselves stay blank (req silent error).

expectations.text: Uploading a file that is not a CSV (e.g. a .txt with random text, or wrong extension) produces a readable message and no R error.
expectations.evidence: notes.txt: read.csv parses it, then showNotification('The file has no numeric columns.') fires; no R error. Message is readable but misleading (does not say the file is not a CSV); no extension check.

suggestions.assertion: The report is rendered from a template copied to tempdir() (or otherwise not written into the app folder) and receives data via params or an explicit environment, not via global variables.
suggestions.reason: Assumes an Rmd/template approach; a run that builds HTML inline in downloadHandler (no template, no params, no app-folder writes, no globals) is ambiguous. Clarify whether inline HTML generation is acceptable.

suggestions.assertion: Code reads input$<file>$datapath and guards with req() so nothing errors before a file is uploaded.
suggestions.reason: Wording requires req(); validate(need(input$file, ...)) is an equivalent (better, message-bearing) guard. Consider 'req() or validate(need())'.

suggestions.assertion: Uploading a file that is not a CSV (e.g. a .txt with random text, or wrong extension) produces a readable message and no R error.
suggestions.reason: A random .txt usually parses as a 1-column CSV, so a generic 'no numeric columns' message satisfies the check; consider requiring the message to identify the wrong file type.

eval_feedback.overall: Both apps work end to end without pandoc. Differences are in error UX and report architecture.
